teaser.text: British American Tobacco is a global nicotine company whose biggest business remains cigarettes, even as it builds products that do not burn tobacco. To understand its business, follow both the products adults repeatedly buy and the money that moves backward through the retail chain.

stock.title: BAT stock forecast
stock.meta_description: BAT stock forecast: weighted scenarios turn positive by October 2029, but depend on cigarette pricing, New Categories and cash conversion.
stock.opening: The weighted price is 4271.32 GBp in October 2029, a 20% gain. It hinges on cigarette pricing holding up while New Categories become repeatable profit and cash.
stock.closing: The full memo also answers how BAT's business works, who its rivals are, how management allocates capital, and what risks could change the scenarios.

blocks.heading: Where could BAT's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted price is 3837.28 GBp in October 2027, a 3% loss including dividends. It is 4271.32 GBp in October 2029, a 20% gain. The bear case carries 25% probability and the base case 55%. The bull case carries 20%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for BAT?

paragraphs.text: In 2025, combustible volume fell 8.1%, but price and mix added 9.1%. New Categories revenue then grew 18.0% at constant currency in the first half of 2026, with a 13.3% contribution margin. The bear case gives earnings of £7,095m, £6,885m and £6,678m as volume decline, price elasticity and cash costs erode margins. The bull case gives £8,010m, £8,596m and £9,261m as Velo and Vuse gain repeat buyers and savings improve profitability. The 2030 margin ambition of 30.0% supports the direction, but not rapid delivery by 2029.

The bear case assumes cigarette volumes fall faster than expected, price rises drive trading down or illicit purchases, and New Categories fail to replace lost contribution. Settlement payments and weaker cash conversion constrain buybacks, while the multiple contracts. It gives 2809.18 GBp in October 2027 and 2359.49 GBp in October 2029. Its 25% probability reflects the 8.1% volume decline, U.S. profit concentration and cash demands, but stable adjusted margins and 2026 growth guidance limit the odds.

blocks.heading: How much cash does BAT really make?

paragraphs.text: Revenue slipped to £25,610m in 2025. Operating margin recovered to 39.0% after -57.7% in 2023. The company’s own free cash flow fell to 14.4% of revenue, and the key number is the 120.96p per-share cash gap between dividends paid and real free cash flow.

dividend.title: BAT dividend: cash cover and yield
dividend.meta_description: BAT's base-case dividend rises, while 2025 free cash flow did not cover dividends; see BAT's cash allocation and current yield.
dividend.opening: BAT's base-case forecast dividend per share rises from £2.475 to £2.575 over the forecast years shown. In 2025, BAT's own free cash flow was £3,790m against £5,238m of dividends, so that cash measure did not cover the dividend.
dividend.closing: The full memo also examines BAT's business, rivals, management choices and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does BAT pay per share over the years shown?

paragraphs.text: Base dividends per share rise from £2.475 to £2.524 and then £2.575. This follows the two latest 2% increases and management’s progressive-dividend policy. The bear case gives £2.45, then £2.39 and £2.33, reflecting recent cash-flow pressure. The bull case gives £2.50, £2.60 and £2.70, requiring stronger cash conversion. Dividends exceeded free cash flow in 2025 and the first half of 2026, so acceleration is not the central assumption.

blocks.heading: Is BAT's dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: - **Settlements and debt.** Canada initially directs 85% of qualifying after-tax income to settlement payments; BAT paid £2,560m upfront in 2025. The company’s own free cash flow was £3,790m against £5,238m of dividends, restricting debt reduction and investment.

paragraphs.text: For 2026, management guides to revenue growth of 3.0–5.0%. It guides to adjusted operating-profit growth of 4.0–6.0% and adjusted diluted EPS growth of 5.0–8.0%, at constant exchange rates and adjusted for Canada where stated. It targets adjusted net debt to adjusted EBITDA of 2.0–2.5x and a £1,300m share buyback in 2026. Horizon 2030 targets New Category contribution margin of at least 30.0%, versus 13.8% in the first half of 2026.

blocks.heading: What is BAT's dividend yield today against its share price?

paragraphs.text: At 4,194.00p on 11 October 2026, one share represents a small ownership interest in BAT. Market value was £90,473.39 million; enterprise value was £122,490.39 million. Enterprise value estimates the operating business belonging to both shareholders and lenders. Like buying a shop with a mortgage, the buyer must account for the debt as well as the price paid to the owner. BAT reported net debt of £32,555 million at 30 June 2026, so lenders have a prior claim on the business.
